title: If we all have access to the same AI tools, what makes our games different?
author: MuhEry22
selftext:
I’m making a game with AI assistance, and something keeps crossing my mind: anyone else can use the same tools and ask for similar mechanics. So what would make my game worth playing over theirs?

I still choose what to build and what to change, but “having ideas” doesn’t feel like much of an advantage when everyone has ideas.

Where do you think the real difference comes from—game feel, art direction, understanding players, or how much time you spend refining things?

What’s something you bring to your game that another person with the same AI tools probably wouldn’t?

comments.author: Honest-Quality-6422
comments.body:
There is such a huge canyon between what you can do with ai and what is possible with ai. This is called the capability overhang and no one is free of it

Every part of your skill and experience will shape what you make, ai is a tool in your tool box, even if it’s with you every step of the way

Unless you are one shotting a prompt to create a replica of something you played or that someone else prompted, your result will be unique to a certain degree

Ai developed assets have certain qualities, some might be able to tell like when Gemini nanobanana came out, the difference from a ChatGPT generated image, or a lot of times you can tell whe html/cas styling has that ChatGPT feel- but just like others have said, we are all painting, we are not just comparing buckets or brushes though

How you approach problems, what questions you ask, what parts of your own taste and judgement you bring to the table, apart from what the model had in its training data and RL, will differentiate your work

There’s some schools of thought that novel results are more than just a combination of what was there before. Even if such results were finite, there are many factors that contribute to the quality of your work

“Ai slop” is a matter not of the tool used, but its method of use.

comments.author: ArtemisWingz
comments.body:
The same thing that has separated other games from eachother before A.I.

Passion, attention, polish, refinement, feel, story, visuals

There is a reason Final Fantasy stands out from generic RPG Maker RPG games even though a lot of the early Final Fantasys could easily be made in RPG Maker.
